name: Native contribution supported by allele-linked, condition-matched organism performance
description: Support a conditioned native contribution through allele-linked physiological performance with exact strain, resources, environment, time window, population and restoration controls.

support.proposition: A defined physiological outcome depends on the gene/activity in a specified strain under explicit resource, environmental, time-window and population conditions, with the actual perturbation and restoration comparisons retained.

operands.instruction: Keep actual allele/strain and organism, resource/medium, atmosphere/host/environment, competition or monoculture, sampling time, population and readout. Distinguish growth, survival/CFU, colonization, recovery and immediate lag. Preserve allele restoration, competitor/host controls and alternative-route genotypes. A matched effect strengthens the conditioned contribution; a matched nonphenotype weakens universal necessity without erasing biochemical capability. observed_extent applies only to actual measured input/source geometry, clipped to original material; target_footprint can restrict that measurement. direct applies only when actual source subjects and the target proposition/conditions match. For another source subject use non-direct applicability. inferred_extent requires an explicit target_footprint bounded by the actual assigned original-input scope; missing target_footprint supplies no invented extent. context_allocation requires explicit context_account_scope and nonempty context_scope on both assessment and compatible account; it cannot carry target_footprint, creates no molecular measurement and is not a sequence map. Source residue numbers never become target coordinates. This measured-extent operand is for actual matching scoped source material only; direct never pairs with inferred_extent. Source facts from another protein/organism instead use the attributed operand.

qualifications: A survival phenotype does not identify a molecular substrate, and nutrient/metal rescue can reflect regulation or bypass. Individual-cell trajectories, pooled reporters and CFU are distinct; no unmeasured lineage relationship is asserted. No tested nonphenotype establishes universal dispensability.

Retain actual source_ref, source_subject_refs, condition_refs and assumption_refs. The published examples below are instruction provenance about their named subjects; they are not observations of ybhP/b0790 and were not repeated to prepare this draft.

At construction and in decision context, resolve these observation kinds through annotation_support_routes for the actual caller-bound annotation policy; an entry does not supply universal component labels, select a projector, mask another kind, change a weight, or create a target finding. An unavailable route declaration remains unavailable.

Use actual retained assessments in a compatible annotation account. Selecting this entry earns nothing. The current caller-owned applicability × relation × extent arithmetic, same-component maximum, coherent-account integration and derived discrimination remain unchanged for this review basis. A finding qualification is not an automatic numeric discount; no independence, confidence or new score dimension is implied.
support.boundary: This route creates no new time/population axis and adopts no physiological effect-size, fitness threshold or acceptance rule. Whether native corroboration should receive a separate numeric dimension remains unresolved; the unchanged actual policy applies. Retain conflicting observations and specific unestablished mechanisms.

evidence.observation: Genetics/metabolomics in tractable P. denitrificans supported catabolism and salt-dependent osmolyte retention.
evidence.limit: Relevant full primary methods/results inspected; supplementary datasets not independently reanalyzed.

evidence.observation: In native Haloferax volcanii, ΔflgA1A2 lost motility while retaining surface adhesion; ΔpibD lost both. Complementation restored the respective phenotypes. Growth/competition controls and processing-dependent mobility changes supported a specific PibD-associated defect. Class I S-layer processing was unaffected.
evidence.limit: Complete relevant Methods/Results and stated observations/captions; no independent filament composition measurement, image analysis, expression quantitation or complete FlaFind rerun. | Source observation limit: Adhesion depended on medium and oxygen context. Candidate pilin shifts and retained adhesion without archaellins suggested additional substrates, but this paper did not identify every native adhesion filament. Its EM could not distinguish the apparatus. Gene deletion phenotypes alone do not identify a direct PibD substrate.

evidence.observation: Authors: actS deletion suppresses lysis of an LPS-transport/ldtF perturbation; direct LdtF control remains unproven.
evidence.limit: Complete primary Results/Discussion/Experimental Procedures inspected. No raw fluorescence, chromatogram or microscopy reanalysis.

evidence.observation: CetZ inactivation does not yield the FtsZ-like division defect. cetZ1 deletion prevents rods at motile halo edges; GTPase-mutant expression and envelope-associated dynamic structures reinforce shape participation.
evidence.limit: Full paper results and extended-data controls inspected; rod/motility relationship is condition dependent. | Group source-use limits: Deletion, dominant mutants and imaging share one study. A motility phenotype does not measure direct motor activity; the tested nonphenotype is not universal absence of division involvement.

evidence.observation: CRISPRi interactions identify envelope dependencies; bamB/dolP double deletion impairs growth and reduces BamA. DolP co-purifies with membrane-assembled BamA and redistributes from midcell under stress.
evidence.limit: Full Results, selected controls and published peer-review limitations inspected; no new phenotyping. | Group source-use limits: Co-purification is not direct binding or catalysis; genetics, purification and imaging are connected results in one study.

evidence.observation: Structure shows a periplasm-length hydrophobic tunnel. Lipid crosslinking places phosphate-bearing material inside it. Length and pore-loop mutants lose ability to complement a sensitized pqiAB/letAB detergent phenotype.
evidence.limit: Full primary Results on architecture, length threshold, pore-loop mutants and crosslinking read. No structural re-refinement. | Group source-use limits: Cryo-EM, crosslinking and complementation are different connected modalities; they are not three direct transport assays. Lipid identity, direction and net flux remain unresolved.

evidence.observation: Lipid-A modification profiles remain unchanged without yhdP. Combined depletion of three AsmA-like proteins is lethal and alters GPL partitioning; adding induced yhdP restores growth. Double mutants release LPS-enriched vesicles.
evidence.limit: Published full Results and lipid/depletion controls examined. The separate 2023 preprint was identified and excluded from published-case evidence. | Group source-use limits: Double/triple-mutant, fractionation and rescue experiments form one redundancy investigation. The separate 2023 preprint was excluded; isolated transport remains unmeasured.

evidence.observation: Deletion is cold-sensitive and accumulates pre50S; cryo-EM resolves immature PTC/H68-H69 states. Domain/loop perturbations and uL16 association distinguish contributions.
evidence.limit: Primary full Results and Fig 1 inspected. No EM image reprocessing. | Group source-use limits: Cryo-EM, gradients and mutants are connected author measurements; no image reprocessing or universal assembly requirement was established.

evidence.observation: Across MCR-containing archaeal genomes, MMP16 tracks sulfoacetaldehyde-biosynthesis genes and often clusters with them. Knockout growth in standard sulfide-containing medium showed a defect rather than absolute auxotrophy. Removing supplied sulfide uncovered CoM-dependent growth; complementation restored it. Methionine inhibition experiments implicated a possible L-ASST backup without proving its mechanism.
evidence.limit: Full genomic, growth, complementation, transcriptomic and cysteine-mutant results, discussion, and phylogenetic methods read. Author data/code not rerun; no purified-enzyme activity claimed. | Group source-use limits: No purified ComF activity or exact L-ASST backup mechanism is claimed. Comparative results and shared strains/media are connected evidence.

evidence.observation: 2010 chemical measurements, genetic competitions, host oxidase perturbations and allele restoration establish an inflammation-dependent intestinal benefit.
evidence.limit: 1999 Results and experimental descriptions; 2010 main Results/Methods Summary and figure captions; live AJ224978.1 metadata verified LT2 ttr locus, 12,121 bp. No raw LC-MS or animal reanalysis. | Group source-use limits: The 1999 and 2010 tests have different recipients/host scopes. The later EutC source also appears in the Ttr detailed trace and remains the same source when reused. Exact in-vivo flux/carbon supply remains unresolved. | This row selects an exact clause from the aggregate retained observation; other source clauses are not attributed to this URL.

evidence.limit: 2012 Results/Methods; 2016 MeDH Results/growth/glassware/assay methods and ExaF Results, tables and assay details. evidence.observation: Deletion/complementation growth matrices separated taurine-specific TauABC uptake from broader SsuABC uptake. Some TauD-reactive compounds entered through SsuABC instead. Low-copy, but not high-copy, tauA/tauB complementation restored taurine growth. Purified SsuD chemistry is reported separately.
evidence.limit: 2000 complete substrate-specificity, deletion-control and complementation Results/Discussion plus Methods descriptions; 1999 biochemical abstract only. 1996 discovery paper is a separate abstract-level lead. | Group source-use limits: The separate 1999 purified SsuD source is abstract-only and is not selected as detailed molecular-activity evidence; the 1996 discovery remains an auxiliary abstract lead. Matrix cells are connected comparisons.

evidence.observation: Clean deletion abolished glycine-only carbon growth, strongly lowered gcs2 transcripts, and removed most broad expression changes reported from an older transposon strain. Promoter reporters responded to glycine; EMSAs established promoter binding.
evidence.limit: Main Results, growth and RNA-seq/accession Methods; live GSE76522 metadata: four RNA-seq samples, two WT/two deletion, SRA SRP068065. No reads reprocessed. | Group source-use limits: GEO metadata are custody/availability information, not an independent RNA-seq experiment. GcsR is a regulator, not a glycine-cleaving enzyme; direct ligand binding remains unknown.

evidence.observation: tcuC loss prevented tricarballylate but not citrate growth in Salmonella. tcuC alone enabled E. coli citrate growth; tcuABC was needed for tricarballylate growth. Point mutations and complementation/marker rescue implicated tcuRABC.
evidence.limit: Complete relevant Results/Discussion and growth methods; no independent transport measurements or enzyme assays performed. | Group source-use limits: The tcuB repair used recombination/marker rescue rather than ordinary complementation. Recipient growth does not directly measure the proposed purified catalytic reactions.

evidence.observation: Whole-locus loss abolished xyloglucan growth. BoGH5A loss was rescued by externally generated xyloglucan oligosaccharides; BoGH9A loss had no tested growth effect. Dietary competition showed a benefit only when alternative polysaccharides were removed.
evidence.limit: Main Results and growth/reverse-genetics Methods, Extended Data captions/tables including dietary competition. No inference that ordinary human diets necessarily select the locus. | Group source-use limits: Product rescue, gene losses and dietary competitions are connected tests. Ordinary human-diet selection and all neighbor requirements are not established.

evidence.observation: Deletion retained whole-cell hopanoids but removed outer-membrane hopanoid localization. At 38 C it impaired growth and caused filamentation; hpnN complementation restored phenotypes. Removing hopanoid synthesis suppressed filamentation, separating mislocalization from simple absence.
evidence.limit: Relevant phylogeny/localization, cell-cycle and temperature Results plus lipid methods; no new localization assay or claim that all RND homologs have this substrate. | Group source-use limits: Connected fractionation, temperature and suppression tests do not measure purified HpnN transport chemistry or justify transfer to every RND homolog.

evidence.observation: Fucose induced the locus and improved growth. Cj0486 restored E. coli fucP function; radiolabeled uptake was lost in its mutant. Piglet competition showed a defect. Poultry effects differed with inoculum, supplementation and competition versus single-strain infection.
evidence.limit: Primary Results/uptake Methods and both papers' poultry Results inspected; no universal chicken-negative or virulence-essential claim. | Group source-use limits: The original string combines two papers and host conditions; neither URL is asserted to independently support every composite clause. No universal chicken-negative or virulence-essential conclusion follows.

evidence.limit: Primary Results/uptake Methods and both papers' poultry Results inspected; no universal chicken-negative or virulence-essential claim. | Group source-use limits: The original string combines two papers and host conditions; neither URL is asserted to independently support every composite clause. evidence.observation: Mucin competitions implicated respiration. A narG napA narZ mutant lacked nitrate reductase activity and lost competitive fitness during colitis. Mucus nitrate increased; host Nos2 loss or iNOS inhibition removed the advantage despite inflammation. Genetic restoration recovered fitness.
evidence.limit: Main Results and figure/method descriptions; no nitrate chemistry or animal experiment repeated. Cofactor moaA phenotype alone was not taken as nitrate-specific evidence. | Group source-use limits: Nitrate chemistry, bacterial restoration and host interventions form linked experimental steps. A triple knockout is not three isolated gene contributions; broad moaA effects are not nitrate-specific.

evidence.observation: Isotope tracing showed methylcitrate accumulation and downstream TCA depletion. Vitamin B12 rerouting restored survival without fully restoring growth; other supplements addressed growth limitations. Purified GlpX was inhibited by methylcitrate.
evidence.limit: Relevant complete Results and culture/extraction Methods; no isotope-flux recomputation. The 2005 infection paper was retrieved but remains an abstract-level auxiliary source here. | Group source-use limits: Metabolomics, rescue and GlpX assays are connected evidence; isotope flux was not recomputed. The auxiliary 2005 infection source remains abstract-only.

evidence.observation: Wild type used pyrimidines for nitrogen at low temperature. Mutants/suppressors separated nitrogen release from toxicity control. RutG loss blocked uracil but not uridine use; in-vitro release of ammonium did not remove in-vivo requirements for RutC-E.
evidence.limit: Complete relevant biochemical, deletion, RutG and toxicity/suppressor Results plus assay/growth Methods; no new suppressed-strain or reaction analysis. | Group source-use limits: In-vitro ammonium release does not demonstrate complete in-vivo sufficiency; not every individual Rut purified activity or temperature-dependent mechanism is established.

evidence.observation: Deletion of either nifI abolished rapid ammonium switch-off of acetylene reduction; complementation restored it. Switching reversed after ammonium removal, without detectable NifH modification/degradation or a nif-mRNA effect. Wild type accelerated growth after ammonium addition; the double mutant did not.
evidence.limit: Main complete switch-off/reversibility/physiology Results and culture/assay Methods; no direct protein-interaction work claimed from this paper. | Group source-use limits: Connected activity and physiological controls do not establish direct physical nitrogenase inhibition or make NifI a catalyst. Negative blot findings retain detection limits.

evidence.observation: malR deletion removed extra growth supported by maltose/dextrin but retained sucrose growth. Locus transcripts and malE reporters fell; reporter activation was restored by MalR coexpression. Purified MalR bound the promoter; adding maltose did not change binding in EMSA.
evidence.limit: Relevant Results including deletion, reporter rescue and sugar-independent DNA binding; growth/deletion/purification Methods inspected. | Group source-use limits: Growth, reporters and EMSA are related system measurements. Sugar-independent EMSA does not rule out every possible ligand-binding/sensing mechanism.

evidence.observation: LC-MS detected copper-yersiniabactin in infected mouse and patient samples. ybtS loss increased copper sensitivity; purified unoccupied yersiniabactin rescued, whereas copper-preloaded ligand did not. Catecholate removal changed copper toxicity in the opposite direction.
evidence.limit: Relevant complete Results and quantitative figure captions; no new patient analysis or purified YbtS catalysis. | Group source-use limits: Patient detection is not an intervention; ligand loading controls are one connected mechanistic test. YbtS is not reassigned as a copper enzyme and universal infection fitness remains unknown.

evidence.observation: D-serine supported defined-medium nutrition. dsd mutants had no significant six-hour growth or competition defect in human/mouse urine ex vivo. dsdA loss nevertheless reduced fitness in a 96-hour catheterized mouse infection, including polymicrobial infections; motility/urease controls were largely retained.
evidence.limit: Relevant growth/urine/motility/CAUTI Results and protocols; no inference that ex-vivo nonphenotype disproves an in-host role. | Group source-use limits: Motility/urease controls were largely retained. Infection counts do not identify catalytic chemistry, and the tested catheterized model does not establish a universal urine-growth defect or complete mechanism.

evidence.observation: A markerless C260V substitution removed excitation quenching in purified IsiA. Under stringent iron deficiency and high light, mutant cells initially grew quickly then bleached/declined; low light avoided bleaching. In iron-replete high light the mutant reached greater density.
evidence.limit: Complete relevant mutant/spectroscopy/growth Results and growth conditions. No new fluorescence-lifetime analysis. | Group source-use limits: Spectroscopy and growth are connected but distinct measurements. Early and late outcomes do not independently support one unconditional benefit; no new lifetime analysis was done.

evidence.observation: eutC had no typhoid-model defect but lost a luminal benefit in colitis. In-vitro ethanolamine growth required tetrathionate; eutC allele/operon restoration rescued. The benefit vanished without inflammation or tetrathionate respiration. Colon ethanolamine concentrations did not explain the condition effect.
evidence.limit: Complete relevant Results and anaerobic-growth/ethanolamine-analysis Methods; no fresh ethanolamine measurement or assertion that eutC phenotype identifies its chemical mechanism by itself. | Group source-use limits: The 2011 source is also used in the Ttr detailed trace and remains the same underlying experiment. These phenotypes do not identify EutC chemistry or every in-vivo Ttr carbon source.

evidence.observation: pdu loss reduced inflammatory-gut fitness. Unlike ethanolamine, ttr loss did not erase benefit; combined aerobic/anaerobic respiratory lesions did. Germ-free mice lacked the benefit, while Bacteroides association restored it and yielded measurable propanediol.
evidence.limit: 2017 relevant full Results and growth/measurement Methods; 2021 initial complete nutrient-growth/expression Results checked. Later glutathione/host mechanism not independently inspected. Grouped as one investigation. | Group source-use limits: The 2017 physiology and initial 2021 regulatory results are connected investigations. The later glutathione/host mechanism was not independently inspected; not every pdu protein receives the system attribution. | This row selects an exact clause from the aggregate retained observation; other source clauses are not attributed to this URL.

evidence.observation: sdhA loss impaired colitis fitness and complementation restored it. Bacteroides-fermented mucin supported uptake-dependent Salmonella growth with nitrate. Bacteroides association restored a transporter benefit absent in germ-free mice, but a succinate-deficient Bacteroides frd mutant did not.
evidence.limit: Relevant complete Results on TCA fitness, uptake and microbial succinate source, plus culture/metabolite Methods; no new flux model or microbiota experiment. | Group source-use limits: Donor mutation, association, metabolite profiles and growth form a connected causal chain rather than independent quantifications of identical flux; no new flux model was run.

evidence.observation: Authors: pxpT or pxpABC loss prevents growth on 5-OP; plasmid pxpT restores its deletion phenotype. This supports uptake involvement but is not direct purified transport measurement.
evidence.limit: Indexed complete relevant regulatory Results, transport Discussion, figure descriptions and culture/purification Methods inspected. Direct publisher fetch 403; raw binding data not obtained. Current published 2026 article used, not 2025 preprint.

evidence.observation: BioJ rescued ΔbioH, hydrolyzed methyl-pimeloyl-ACP with product mass support and restored DTB synthesis in extracts. Catalytic-triad mutants impaired native growth/host replication; biotin relieved defects.
evidence.limit: Relevant complete Results/Methods inspected; no cultures, hosts or quantitative figures reanalyzed.

evidence.observation: Purified MTH1152 transferred GMP to AdoCbi-P but lacked detected AdoCbi kinase activity. cobY rescued de-novo-dependent Salmonella cobU deficiency, but not aerobic cobinamide-salvage demand.
evidence.limit: Complete main Results and relevant Methods read; reported assay negatives remain condition-bounded.

evidence.observation: Some D27G trajectories regained supplement independence via G27C; other evolved lineages retained supplement dependence and accumulated thyA/deoB loss mutations.
evidence.limit: Relevant full Results/Methods and figure descriptions read; no evolution, raw sequencing or omics reanalysis.

evidence.observation: Synechocystis HemG substitution supported glucose growth but failed photoautotrophic growth with altered intermediates. Purified heme-bound HemJ lacked detectable PPO activity in tested assays.
evidence.limit: Complete relevant Results read in both studies; interaction/coupling interpretation retained as hypothesis.

evidence.observation: Later K12 experiments found no ΔlysU growth difference; ΔlysU and ΔlysS grew similarly across tested temperatures and rich/minimal media.
evidence.limit: 1990 abstract plus complete relevant 2017 primary Results subsection read; conflicting conditions were not experimentally reconciled.

evidence.observation: Native Mtb deletion work found no inositol requirement in recovered cysQ mutants but explicitly could not exclude acquired suppressors.
evidence.limit: 2008 primary relevant full methods/results/discussion inspected. 2010 CysQ deletion, extract-activity and discussion sections inspected; no genome analysis of putative suppressors.

evidence.observation: Under alpha-methylglucoside stress, a yigL deletion was disadvantaged in minimal glycerol medium; requirements differed with medium and stressor.
evidence.limit: 2024 relevant complete results/discussion and assay/genotype methods inspected; 2013 relevant regulation, competition and growth results inspected. Supplements not independently analyzed. Fresh public-record probe documented in raw/live_probe_summary.json.

evidence.observation: Follow-up reproduced the salvage contribution with casamino-acid enrichment, but saw little effect in un-enriched minimal medium; dgt supplied an alternative route.
evidence.limit: 2007 salvage relevant whole results and media methods; 2011 relevant dgt/yjjG comparisons, discussion and medium composition inspected. 2007 housecleaning primary abstract only; publisher PDF access failed.

evidence.observation: Ammonium-limited cultures showed yeaG induction. Deletion shortened recovery lag and reduced metabolic heterogeneity yet accelerated viability loss after prolonged starvation; wild-type complementation restored survival. Catalytic-domain variants failed to rescue.
evidence.limit: Relevant complete Results subsections on induction/recovery, viability and heterogeneity; culture and CFU methods. No reanalysis of cytometry files. | Group source-use limits: cellular_yeaG and organism_06_yeag duplicate the same 2015 study; their source identity must be shared. The 2021 workbook retains its exact original lineage. Keep the further-72h versus 24h caption inconsistency, delta-yeaH/delta-yeaGH labels and 2021 table-count/SodB-SodA inconsistencies. Missing ratios are not zero phosphorylation.
